note: Authored by reading Tafsir al-Tabari in English against the reader's modern translation. Each phrase carries the app's own words for that piece of the verse, a plain modern English line of my own, the Arabic of the piece, and the numbered paragraphs of the commentary that speak of it.

phrases.translation: Has the news of the Overwhelming Event reached you ˹O Prophet˺
phrases.text: Has the news of the Overwhelming reached you, O Muhammad? The commentators differed: some said it means the resurrection, some the Fire that swallows the faces of the unbelievers. Tabari keeps it general, because both are an overwhelming, and God did not say which one he meant.

phrases.translation: On that Day ˹some˺ faces will be downcast
phrases.text: On that day the faces of those who disbelieved will be abased, humbled in the Fire.

phrases.translation: ˹totally˺ overburdened, exhausted
phrases.text: Those faces will toil in the Fire and be worn out there. The commentators say this is the reward of anyone who was too proud to obey God in this world.

phrases.translation: burning in a scorching Fire
phrases.text: These faces will enter a blazing Fire whose heat has become intense. The reciters differ on the reading here, and Tabari says both readings are correct in meaning.

phrases.translation: left to drink from a scalding spring
phrases.text: They will be given to drink from a spring whose heat has reached its utmost, and has been boiling since the day God created the heavens and the earth. Some said the word simply means the spring is there, ready and waiting.

phrases.translation: They will have no food except a foul, thorny shrub
phrases.text: Their only food is the thorn plant, and it is poison. The commentators say it is the shibriq bush when it is withered, some say it is stone, and some say it is a thorn of fire. It is the worst and most foulest of food.
phrases.ar: لَّيۡسَ لَهُمۡ طَعَامٌ إِلَّا مِن ضَرِيعٖ

phrases.translation: neither nourishing nor satisfying hunger
phrases.text: That thorn does not give the one who eats it any nourishment, and it does not take the edge off his hunger.
phrases.ar: لَّا يُسۡمِنُ وَلَا يُغۡنِي مِن جُوعٖ

phrases.translation: On that Day ˹other˺ faces will be glowing with bliss
phrases.text: And on that day other faces will be joyful, radiant with the grace God grants His people in the gardens. These are the believers.

phrases.translation: ˹fully˺ pleased with their striving
phrases.text: God is well pleased with the work they did in obedience to Him in this world, and also with the reward He gives them for it in the hereafter.

phrases.translation: in an elevated Garden
phrases.text: They are in a lofty garden, that is, an orchard set high.

phrases.translation: where no idle talk will be heard
phrases.text: There they will hear no idle talk, meaning no word that is empty or false, and no abusive speech. The reciters differ on the reading, and Tabari holds that all the well-known readings carry a sound meaning.

phrases.translation: In it will be a running spring
phrases.text: In the garden there is a spring that flows freely, without a channel to carry it.

phrases.translation: along with thrones raised high
phrases.text: And couches raised high, so that as the believer sits on one he can take in all the bounty and the kingdom his Lord has given him. Some said they are set close together, one above another.

phrases.translation: and cups set at hand
phrases.text: And goblets standing ready, and these are cups with no handles. They are set at the edge of the flowing spring, so that whenever the guest wants to drink he finds them filled.

phrases.translation: and ˹fine˺ cushions lined up
phrases.text: And cushions set in a row, and these are the cushions and the armrest cushions. They are set in rows because they stand next to one another.

phrases.translation: and ˹splendid˺ carpets spread out
phrases.text: And carpets spread out, many rugs with a fine thin pile. Umar once prayed on one of these rugs.

phrases.translation: Do they not ever reflect on camels—how they were ˹masterfully˺ created
phrases.text: Do these people, who deny God's power over the punishment and the bliss He has described, never look at the camel and see how He made it, made it obedient, and made it kneel and rise with its load? The One who made that can make what He has described of Paradise and the Fire.
phrases.ar: أَفَلَا يَنظُرُونَ إِلَى ٱلۡإِبِلِ كَيۡفَ خُلِقَتۡ

phrases.translation: and the sky—how it was raised ˹high˺
phrases.text: Do they not also look at the sky and see how He raised it up, so that they may know that His power is not hindered from doing anything He wants to do.

phrases.translation: and the mountains—how they were firmly set up
phrases.text: And the mountains, how He set them upright so that they do not fall and spread over the earth, but stand firm in their place and do not move from their spot.

phrases.translation: and the earth—how it was levelled out
phrases.text: And the earth, how He levelled it flat. Then the question is asked: is the One who made this not able to make whatever He wills in the Garden?

phrases.translation: So, ˹continue to˺ remind ˹all, O Prophet˺, for your duty is only to remind
phrases.text: So remind, O Muhammad, My servants with My signs, warn them with My proofs and pass on My message. You are only a reminder: I sent you to remind them of My favour to them, to make known what is required of them, and to warn them.

phrases.translation: You are not ˹there˺ to compel them ˹to believe˺
phrases.text: You have no power over them, and you are not one who forces people to what he wants. Leave them to God and to His judgment of them.

phrases.translation: But whoever turns away, persisting in disbelief
phrases.text: Except whoever turns away from you and from the signs of God and so becomes an unbeliever. This can also be read as a separate statement, so that it means: you have no power over them, and whoever turns away and disbelieves, him God will punish.

phrases.translation: then Allah will inflict upon them the major punishment
phrases.text: God will punish him with the greatest punishment, which is the punishment of Hell, for his unbelief in this world and for the punishment of the hereafter.

phrases.translation: Surely to Us is their return
phrases.text: Their return is to Us. This tells the Prophet that the punishing is God's work and not his, and that his task is only to admonish and to pass on the message.

phrases.translation: then surely with Us is their reckoning
phrases.text: And the reckoning is with Us, for God will requite every man for the disobedience he committed against his Lord.
